editorial:
Imagine being a rich kid with everything you could ever want, except for a little brother to play with. That is exactly where you find Joe Cobb, a wealthy boy who is desperate for a sibling. When his nurse takes him to meet the Our Gang kids, things get wild very quickly. The vibe is pure old-school chaos. You get to see these kids try to run a business by selling babies to Joe for a few bucks. It is a funny, lighthearted look at how kids think they can solve adult problems with simple, silly plans. 

What really stands out is the creativity of the baby assembly line. Watching them wash and feed babies like they are in a factory is the best part of the movie. While the pacing is a bit slow by today's standards, the physical comedy keeps you grinning. If you enjoy classic silent films, you should definitely grab this on a 4K Blu-ray for your physical collection to see the details clearly. Otherwise, renting it on Apple TV is a great way to experience this vintage charm without spending too much money.
endingExplained: The chaos peaks when Joe realizes the baby he bought is not actually his brother. The twist comes from the funny way Farina tried to make the baby fit Joe's expectations by painting him white. Once the truth comes out, the makeshift baby factory falls apart. Everything wraps up with the kids learning that you cannot just buy a sibling from a gang of neighborhood children, leaving you with a big laugh.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves classic silent comedies and cute kids causing trouble.
